title: Relation Between Refractive Indices
notes: **Absolute refractive index:** measured relative to vacuum or air. $n_{abs} = c/v_{medium}$.
**Relative refractive index:** $n_{21} = n_2/n_1 = v_1/v_2$. This is the ratio of speeds in the two media.
**Reciprocity:** $n_{12} = 1/n_{21}$. The index of medium 2 relative to 1 is the reciprocal of the index of medium 1 relative to 2.
**Additivity rule:** for a stack of parallel slabs, the overall lateral shift depends on the sum of individual shifts. The relative indices multiply along the path.
**Practical example:** light going air ($n_1=1$) to water ($n_2=1.33$) to glass ($n_3=1.52$): $n_{13} = n_3/n_1 = 1.52$, but the effective path depends on each interface separately.
